relevance.rationale: Defines the extended Bloch group Bhat(C), proves lambda : H_3(PSL(2,C)^delta; Z) -> Bhat(C) is an isomorphism, and shows the extended Rogers dilogarithm Rhat descends so that R o lambda is the Cheeger--Chern--Simons class, i(vol + i cs) in C/pi^2 Z. Two distinct corpus artifacts depend on precisely this and neither cites it. (1) docs/audits/2026-08-07-extended-bloch-group-fixes-the-normalization-fit.md (dated one day before this triage, PR #4664) builds its whole argument on 'the extended Bloch group is the canonical resolution of the branch-of-logarithm ambiguity' and even quotes Rhat(betahat(M)) = Vol + i CS; the audit itself notes the phrase 'extended Bloch' occurs in exactly one corpus file. This is the source and it has no bibliographic entry. (2) conj:borromean-bloch-group-element states as a CONJECTURE that the Borromean rings complement determines a non-trivial Bloch-group element whose regulator is Vol(B_3) = 8G. Its hypotheses -- complete, finite-volume, hyperbolic 3-manifold -- hold for the Borromean complement (two ideal regular octahedra, volume 8G), so Sec. 1 and Sec. 14 of this document supply the existence, and non-triviality follows because the regulator is non-zero. What this document does NOT supply is the conjecture's second clause, the claim that the Markov-trace coefficient h^4 = -3/4 has a 'K-theoretic shadow' equal to (8G)(-3/4) = -6G; that clause is an unsupported multiplication of two numbers and must stay open. So the conjecture as written bundles a standard theorem with an unproved numerical claim, and only the first half is discharged.

keyResults.statement: Any complete hyperbolic 3-manifold of finite volume carries a natural fundamental class in H_3(PSL(2,C); Z) determining an element betahat(M) in the extended Bloch group, and R o lambda computes the Cheeger--Chern--Simons class i(vol(M) + i cs(M)).
keyResults.useForFolio: Discharges the existence-and-regulator clause of conj:borromean-bloch-group-element for the Borromean complement, whose hypotheses are met; the residual open content is then only the h^4 = -3/4 shadow claim.

keyResults.locator: Sec. 1, 'Roger's dilogarithm function' map R : Bhat(C) -> C/pi^2 Z
keyResults.statement: The extended Rogers dilogarithm is well defined modulo pi^2 Z on flattened shape parameters, giving the complex volume exactly where the ordinary Bloch group determines the Chern--Simons invariant only up to an additive ambiguity.
keyResults.useForFolio: This is the derived-not-chosen datum the corpus's normalization-route argument needs; citing it converts that argument's central assertion from an uncited claim into a sourced theorem.

proposedActions.rationale: A live audit and an in-flight PR argument rest on this construction with no bibliographic entry anywhere in the corpus.

Hypotheses checked: the theorem requires a complete, finite-volume hyperbolic 3-manifold; the Borromean rings complement satisfies all three. The existence and regulator clause of the conjecture is therefore a corollary, and the block should be re-scoped so that only the h^4 = -3/4 shadow claim remains conjectural. Scope note: this discharges clause 1 only and asserts nothing about clause 2.

The corpus's quantum Bloch group blocks develop the Phi_q pentagon without recording that the CLASSICAL side already has a canonical branch-resolving lift; a remark tying the flattening data to the corpus's fibre-vs-archimedean Im(q) distinction would prevent the branch ambiguity being rediscovered a third time.
